note: Not active; staged editorial question bank pending approved MAIC PDF registration and independent academic review.

questions.stem: Which principle remains unchanged when news moves to digital platforms?
options: Virality becomes a substitute for accuracy
Headlines no longer require source checks
Claims still need evidence and verification
Corrections are unnecessary for short posts
questions.rationale: Digital formats do not reduce the obligation to verify. Source: MAIC Understanding Digital Journalism, page 2.

questions.stem: What is a sensible learning outcome for digital journalism?
options: Invent eyewitness quotes using AI
Trace online claims to primary records and explain uncertainty
Maximize notifications regardless of evidence
Keep all editorial changes unrecorded
questions.rationale: The course teaches online source tracing and careful publication. Source: MAIC Understanding Digital Journalism, page 2.

questions.stem: Which formats may distribute the same verified story?
options: Web text, audio, video and short social updates
Only printed newspapers
Only private staff notes
Only anonymous message screenshots
questions.rationale: Digital journalism uses multiple public channels. Source: MAIC Understanding Digital Journalism, page 2.

questions.stem: What should a short social alert preserve from a full article?
options: Every background paragraph verbatim
The most emotional adjective
Only the article's promotional image
Essential qualifications affecting the truth of its claim
questions.rationale: Compression must not distort the supported conclusion. Source: MAIC Understanding Digital Journalism, page 2.

questions.stem: What is the difference between user engagement and public value?
options: High views always establish truth
Attention data does not itself prove informational usefulness
Public value can only be measured in clicks
Engagement metrics are official fact checks
questions.rationale: Audience signals do not substitute for veracity. Source: MAIC Understanding Digital Journalism, page 2.

questions.stem: Why are updates and correction practices part of digital publishing?
options: A digital page is never revised
News pages can change while earlier versions remain influential
All errors disappear from readers' memories
Social posts are automatically synchronized with articles
questions.rationale: Versioning and corrections preserve accountability. Source: MAIC Understanding Digital Journalism, page 2.

questions.stem: Which skill is relevant to a video posted without a timestamp?
options: Adding cinematic effects to increase realism
Checking provenance, context and original source
Assuming the clip was recorded today
Treating comments as documentary proof
questions.rationale: Digital verification includes source and event context. Source: MAIC Understanding Digital Journalism, page 2.

questions.stem: Why should a digital newsroom plan privacy safeguards?
options: Privacy concerns apply only to paper archives
Public URLs make all identities safe to disclose
A high view count removes all harm risk
Online distribution can expose sensitive personal data widely
questions.rationale: Privacy and security are part of ethical reporting. Source: MAIC Understanding Digital Journalism, page 2.

questions.stem: What is an appropriate role for AI in a digital reporting workflow?
options: Generate a fictional quote and assign it to a real source
Assist drafting or transcription with human source verification
Replace the original evidence with a model summary
Automatically publish unreviewed claims
questions.rationale: AI can support workflow but cannot provide invented reportage. Source: MAIC Understanding Digital Journalism, page 2.

questions.stem: How should a learner interpret a practice rubric?
options: As automatic approval to publish an exam
As evidence every case is real
As feedback, not an official certificate or verified passing grade
As a substitute for source documents
questions.rationale: Practice assessment is distinct from official credentialing. Source: MAIC Understanding Digital Journalism, page 2.

questions.stem: What can a first verified news alert communicate?
options: An unsupported cause stated as certain
Only the most widely shared rumor
An invented eyewitness account
Known practical instructions and current uncertainty
questions.rationale: Early reporting can be useful if evidence boundaries are clear. Source: MAIC Understanding Digital Journalism, page 3.

questions.stem: What must a live news page do when important facts change?
options: Silently deny earlier statements existed
Retain every known mistake without correction
Replace the primary record with an ad
Show meaningful update timing and clarify changed claims
questions.rationale: Revision transparency is important in developing stories. Source: MAIC Understanding Digital Journalism, page 3.

questions.stem: Why must a social preview be independently checked for accuracy?
options: Previews are always private
Many readers may see it without opening the article
Search engines validate the preview automatically
Preview text is never factual
questions.rationale: A fragment can create a false impression. Source: MAIC Understanding Digital Journalism, page 3.

questions.stem: What makes a temporary route-diversion alert useful?
options: Exact affected stops and start time supported by the authority
The reporter's guess about permanent service changes
An unverified explanation of political motives
A dramatic unrelated photo
questions.rationale: Public-service details should be actionable and verified. Source: MAIC Understanding Digital Journalism, page 3.

questions.stem: What is a risk of repeating viral rumors during breaking news?
options: Every repost independently corroborates the event
Repetition can amplify an unsupported central allegation
Popularity proves an authority issued a notice
Virality eliminates the need for timestamps
questions.rationale: Distribution is not confirmation. Source: MAIC Understanding Digital Journalism, page 3.

questions.stem: What belongs in a follow-up after a verified initial alert?
options: An invented explanation for an unresolved cause
Newly checked context attributed to relevant sources
A more alarming version of the same rumor
An identical headline without update information
questions.rationale: Developing coverage should add verified information. Source: MAIC Understanding Digital Journalism, page 3.

questions.stem: How can a newsroom distinguish a provisional statement from a finding?
options: Use the same categorical language for all claims
Label what is known, unknown and under investigation
Omit original source dates
Choose the strongest possible verb
questions.rationale: Status and certainty must be explicit. Source: MAIC Understanding Digital Journalism, page 3.

questions.stem: What should guide priority when a digital story is urgent?
options: Only follower count
Only sponsor preferences
Potential practical public benefit and strength of evidence
Only use of trending music
questions.rationale: Urgency and public value should shape publication. Source: MAIC Understanding Digital Journalism, page 3.

questions.stem: Why should an alert have a reliable source reference?
options: Links make every story automatically true
Readers may need to act before seeing a full report
A source reference replaces checking the document
Short alerts are never corrected
questions.rationale: Primary citations aid verification and use. Source: MAIC Understanding Digital Journalism, page 3.

questions.stem: When should a developing story be updated as a new factual finding?
options: When unverified reposts reach a chosen count
After meaningful confirmation, with clear timing
Immediately after a source speculates
Only when a headline needs more clicks
questions.rationale: Updates should reflect verified developments. Source: MAIC Understanding Digital Journalism, page 3.

questions.stem: What are the five broad stages of a digital news workflow?
options: Gather, verify, edit, publish and monitor
Advertise, publish, invent, delete and deny
Publish, speculate, promote, ignore and replace
Share, count likes, headline, schedule and hide
questions.rationale: A structured workflow separates evidence checks from publication. Source: MAIC Understanding Digital Journalism, page 4.

questions.stem: Why assign a person to caption review?
options: A caption has no factual content
Captions can misstate the event even with genuine footage
The platform always checks dates automatically
Only the photographer needs to inspect a caption
questions.rationale: Multimedia claims require editorial responsibility. Source: MAIC Understanding Digital Journalism, page 4.

questions.stem: What should editorial metadata record?
options: Only the article's font selection
Only the number of reactions
Responsible desk, date, references and publication status
Only the author's preferred emoji
questions.rationale: Metadata assists traceability and updates. Source: MAIC Understanding Digital Journalism, page 4.

questions.stem: What does an accurate revision history allow?
options: Editors to distinguish earlier published text from later correction
A newsroom to conceal past factual errors
A headline to be changed with no record
All source material to be discarded
questions.rationale: Version control supports correction accountability. Source: MAIC Understanding Digital Journalism, page 4.

questions.stem: Why can a content management system not replace an editor?
options: CMS software automatically verifies every interview
Data entry guarantees no misleading statements
Every upload is already publication-ready
Software cannot independently determine if allegations are adequately supported
questions.rationale: Technology assists process but not editorial judgment. Source: MAIC Understanding Digital Journalism, page 4.

questions.stem: What is an important prepublication question?
options: Is the headline longer than every caption?
Does the illustration use the newest color?
Will the story receive a guaranteed number of clicks?
Does the headline make a stronger claim than the supporting evidence?
questions.rationale: Editorial checks evaluate factual support. Source: MAIC Understanding Digital Journalism, page 4.

questions.stem: Which content should trigger proportionately higher review?
options: A routine service-hour notice with clear original evidence
A simple photograph of an empty public building
A correction of a typographic heading
A serious claim involving identifiable people or public safety
questions.rationale: Potential harm determines review intensity. Source: MAIC Understanding Digital Journalism, page 4.

questions.stem: Why should a small newsroom still define review stages?
options: Small teams cannot make reporting errors
Team size automatically prevents bias
Every stage is redundant without a large staff
One person handling several roles still needs explicit checks
questions.rationale: Role consolidation must not erase verification safeguards. Source: MAIC Understanding Digital Journalism, page 4.

questions.stem: What should a responsible correction path specify?
options: Who can identify, verify, document and publish the correction
Only the graphics team
Only the number of readers affected
Only an internal deadline with no action owner
questions.rationale: Corrections need clear workflow ownership. Source: MAIC Understanding Digital Journalism, page 4.

questions.stem: Which item helps verify a video and article concern the same event?
options: Matching original timestamps, locations and documented context
Matching background music
Matching file extensions
Matching number of views
questions.rationale: Cross-format provenance prevents misleading pairing. Source: MAIC Understanding Digital Journalism, page 4.

questions.stem: Why find the earliest traceable online source?
options: It may reveal original context and the claim's evidence chain
First uploaders are always truthful
Older posts are automatically false
Follower count determines authenticity
questions.rationale: Source tracing helps test the claim's origin. Source: MAIC Understanding Digital Journalism, page 5.

questions.stem: Why does a repeated online claim not gain independent proof from reposts?
options: All copies can derive from one unsupported assertion
Each copy creates new firsthand evidence
A different website is always independent
Reposts carry authenticated metadata by default
questions.rationale: Copying does not corroborate content. Source: MAIC Understanding Digital Journalism, page 5.

questions.stem: Which question should be asked about a viral bridge photo?
options: Does the photo have enough dramatic smoke?
When and where was the original image recorded?
How can the headline be more alarming?
How many reactions use fire emojis?
questions.rationale: Date and place must be checked. Source: MAIC Understanding Digital Journalism, page 5.

questions.stem: What could prove a current-fire caption misleading even if the photograph is genuine?
options: It was taken with a phone
It has a high resolution
The photo was originally published years earlier for another event
It contains a recognizable bridge
questions.rationale: Authenticity of pixels does not prove a current-event label. Source: MAIC Understanding Digital Journalism, page 5.

questions.stem: Why should a reporter seek the full video rather than an excerpt?
options: Editing may remove actions or context that change meaning
Full recordings automatically prove every interpretation
Short videos are always fabricated
Audio alone establishes the cause
questions.rationale: Context is required before assigning meaning. Source: MAIC Understanding Digital Journalism, page 5.

questions.stem: What belongs in an online source log?
options: Only follower growth
URL, access date, claims, checks and unresolved questions
Only a guessed political motive
Only an attractive screenshot
questions.rationale: Documentation supports repeatable verification. Source: MAIC Understanding Digital Journalism, page 5.

questions.stem: If a viral post disappears, what is still unproven?
options: That a copy was previously visible
That the journalist inspected the page
That an access timestamp was recorded
That its substantive allegation was accurate
questions.rationale: The existence of a claim differs from its truth. Source: MAIC Understanding Digital Journalism, page 5.

questions.stem: Why should independent evidence verify an image's supposed location?
options: Street signs can never be useful
Visual resemblance can lead to mistaken geographic identification
All bridges look identical
The uploader's city field guarantees authenticity
questions.rationale: Geolocation requires appropriate context and corroboration. Source: MAIC Understanding Digital Journalism, page 5.

questions.stem: What is a proportionate response to a serious online accusation lacking original evidence?
options: Hold it as unverified and seek primary and independent confirmation
Publish it as the headline immediately
Remove all mention of the uncertainty
Describe the accused person as guilty
questions.rationale: Serious claims demand stronger verification. Source: MAIC Understanding Digital Journalism, page 5.

questions.stem: What is a key limit of archived screenshots?
options: They may preserve content but not establish its underlying truth
They always validate the uploader's statements
They automatically show every page revision
They guarantee consent to republish private details
questions.rationale: Archives document appearance, not truth. Source: MAIC Understanding Digital Journalism, page 5.

questions.stem: What should be established about user-generated footage before editorial use?
options: Creator, time, location, context and appropriate rights
Only the uploader's display picture
Only video resolution
Only number of comments
questions.rationale: User footage needs provenance and permissions assessment. Source: MAIC Understanding Digital Journalism, page 6.

questions.stem: Does a public social post automatically confer unrestricted republication rights?
options: Yes, any image online is public domain
Yes, if the uploader has over 100 followers
No, access and permission are distinct legal questions
No rights review is ever relevant to journalism
questions.rationale: Public availability is not the same as reuse authorization. Source: MAIC Understanding Digital Journalism, page 6.

questions.stem: What does a watermark by itself establish about authorship?
options: It is a clue, not conclusive proof of creator identity
It guarantees the file was filmed by the account
It proves that no editing occurred
It supplies accurate GPS location
questions.rationale: Profile branding cannot alone prove ownership. Source: MAIC Understanding Digital Journalism, page 6.

questions.stem: What can a genuine crowd video fail to establish?
options: That the clip shows visible people
The reason the crowd assembled
That the camera recorded a scene
That the clip has duration
questions.rationale: Observation of a crowd is not proof of cause. Source: MAIC Understanding Digital Journalism, page 6.

questions.stem: Why ask contributors for the original file when safe and feasible?
options: It gives the newsroom automatic ownership
It eliminates privacy considerations
It guarantees every spoken assertion is true
It can preserve context and support provenance checks
questions.rationale: Original material strengthens verification. Source: MAIC Understanding Digital Journalism, page 6.

questions.stem: What ethical concern arises when identifying a minor in submitted video?
options: An automatic increase in story importance
Potential privacy and safety harm
All footage becomes unusable forever
A guarantee of legitimate public interest
questions.rationale: Vulnerable identities require heightened care. Source: MAIC Understanding Digital Journalism, page 6.

questions.stem: Why should an editor check what happened before and after a viral excerpt?
options: Events outside the clip never matter
The uploader always explains all context
A short clip can distort the full sequence
Editing cannot alter meaning
questions.rationale: Chronological context matters to interpretation. Source: MAIC Understanding Digital Journalism, page 6.

questions.stem: Which is the correct label for a commuter's own testimony?
options: A complete measured record of all platform usage
Proof of system-wide negligence
A firsthand account of what that person experienced
An audited technical explanation
questions.rationale: Experience and population-level findings differ. Source: MAIC Understanding Digital Journalism, page 6.

questions.stem: What should a caption avoid doing with a user's interpretation?
options: Attributing it to the user
Clarifying that evidence is incomplete
Separating observation from inference
Presenting it as an independently verified factual conclusion
questions.rationale: Interpretation cannot be silently upgraded into fact. Source: MAIC Understanding Digital Journalism, page 6.

questions.stem: What verification question is distinct from whether a file is genuine?
options: Does it actually support the event interpretation assigned to it?
Can it be opened on a device?
Does it have a file extension?
Can its resolution be measured?
questions.rationale: Authenticity and interpretation are separate questions. Source: MAIC Understanding Digital Journalism, page 6.

questions.stem: What is the best reason for including a wide establishing shot?
options: It automatically confirms the cause of the event
It removes the need to check dates
It shows setting and helps preserve spatial context
It guarantees every nearby person consents
questions.rationale: Contextual framing supports interpretation. Source: MAIC Understanding Digital Journalism, page 7.

questions.stem: Why should a mobile reporter record the capture time and place?
options: They make every statement in footage true
They eliminate any need for captions
They guarantee the clip is publishable
Those details help verify when and where the footage was made
questions.rationale: Provenance is part of reliable reporting. Source: MAIC Understanding Digital Journalism, page 7.

questions.stem: What is the priority when recording a spoken interview?
options: A dramatic soundtrack
Intelligible audio and appropriate consent conditions
The largest possible camera zoom
A background that suggests a different location
questions.rationale: Clear source speech is more important than effects. Source: MAIC Understanding Digital Journalism, page 7.

questions.stem: Why may selective cropping be editorially misleading?
options: Every crop is inherently prohibited
It always improves audience comprehension
It can make crowd size or physical conditions appear different
It changes all verified dates automatically
questions.rationale: Camera framing affects apparent context. Source: MAIC Understanding Digital Journalism, page 7.

questions.stem: What does B-roll legitimately do?
options: Replace all missing eyewitness evidence
Illustrate relevant details without pretending to document another event
Show a false chronology without disclosure
Prove an unverified cause
questions.rationale: Illustrative footage must remain correctly labeled. Source: MAIC Understanding Digital Journalism, page 7.

questions.stem: Why retain original video alongside an edited package?
options: It guarantees all sources are independent
It replaces attribution and captioning
It allows checking whether the edit changed the event's meaning
It eliminates the need for a script
questions.rationale: Original media supports accountability. Source: MAIC Understanding Digital Journalism, page 7.

questions.stem: What should a multimedia caption clarify?
options: Only which filter was used
Only the size of the video file
What is shown and which source supports the contextual claim
Only the reporter's preferred camera
questions.rationale: Captions make factual claims too. Source: MAIC Understanding Digital Journalism, page 7.

questions.stem: When can a park-gate video prove the park's official closure reason?
options: Only when the cause is independently established by appropriate records
Whenever the gate appears shut
When the video is in high definition
When many people share the footage
questions.rationale: Visual closure does not establish official reasons. Source: MAIC Understanding Digital Journalism, page 7.

questions.stem: Why should digital news include subtitles where practical?
options: They authenticate every speaker's identity
They establish GPS coordinates
They improve comprehension and accessibility
They eliminate transcription review
questions.rationale: Accessibility broadens access to verified information. Source: MAIC Understanding Digital Journalism, page 7.

questions.stem: Which editing choice is unacceptable without disclosure?
options: Removing clearly irrelevant silence without changing meaning
Adding a truthful source label
Reordering shots to imply actions occurred in a different sequence
Adjusting volume to make speech audible
questions.rationale: Misleading chronology distorts what footage supports. Source: MAIC Understanding Digital Journalism, page 7.

questions.stem: What is a useful web headline for a temporary policy change?
options: A precise statement of the change, timing and status
A vague phrase promising a shocking secret
A categorical accusation before checking facts
A long list of repeated search keywords
questions.rationale: Clear headings support readers and accurate discovery. Source: MAIC Understanding Digital Journalism, page 8.

questions.stem: Why should search-oriented writing avoid keyword stuffing?
options: It can distort meaning and reduce clarity
More repetition always improves verification
Search terms prove source authenticity
Headlines need no relation to article content
questions.rationale: Discoverability must not compromise accuracy. Source: MAIC Understanding Digital Journalism, page 8.

questions.stem: What is the function of descriptive subheadings in a long web article?
options: Make every source independent
Help readers locate relevant supported details
Replace original documentation
Allow an unsupported claim to remain in a headline
questions.rationale: Structure improves navigation without changing evidence. Source: MAIC Understanding Digital Journalism, page 8.

questions.stem: Which link most directly supports a reported official notice?
options: An unrelated commercial landing page
An unattributed social repost
A relevant primary record when safe and legal to share
A link revealing confidential witness addresses
questions.rationale: Primary links make the evidence inspectable. Source: MAIC Understanding Digital Journalism, page 8.

questions.stem: Why must a social preview maintain context?
options: Some readers see the preview without the full article
Only the full article is ever shared
Preview text cannot mislead
A preview is always just decoration
questions.rationale: Fragments can independently convey factual claims. Source: MAIC Understanding Digital Journalism, page 8.

questions.stem: Which accessibility practice helps someone unable to view an image?
options: Replacing all text with decorative color
Using an uncaptioned animation
Hiding the article title in the image
Accurate alternative text describing relevant content
questions.rationale: Alt text can convey content nonvisually. Source: MAIC Understanding Digital Journalism, page 8.

questions.stem: What is wrong with conveying warnings by red and green colors alone?
options: Color contrast has no relation to comprehension
All readers perceive colors identically
Only video requires accessibility
Some readers may miss the difference without textual labels
questions.rationale: Critical distinctions should not depend solely on color. Source: MAIC Understanding Digital Journalism, page 8.

questions.stem: How should meaningful corrections be reflected on a web page?
options: By silently changing the headline only
By deleting all original records
By leaving false snippets unaddressed
With updated information, a visible note and relevant timing
questions.rationale: Transparent revisions support understanding. Source: MAIC Understanding Digital Journalism, page 8.

questions.stem: What should an accessible video package provide where feasible?
options: Only dramatic background music
Only a file without contextual description
Only a promotional image
Readable captions or a transcript
questions.rationale: Captions and transcripts improve usable access. Source: MAIC Understanding Digital Journalism, page 8.

questions.stem: Which web-description claim is unacceptable?
options: One that names the published article topic
One that implies certainty absent from the verified story
One that states the source of a notice
One that accurately identifies a date
questions.rationale: Descriptions must be as evidence-based as the article. Source: MAIC Understanding Digital Journalism, page 8.

questions.stem: Does high page-view count establish that a story is factual?
options: No, it measures attention rather than truth
Yes, every visitor independently verified the facts
Only if social shares are also high
Yes, when the title is short
questions.rationale: Analytics cannot replace journalistic verification. Source: MAIC Understanding Digital Journalism, page 9.

questions.stem: What is necessary before comparing two completion rates?
options: Compatible definitions, populations and reporting periods
The same headline font
Matching cover images
Identical story word counts
questions.rationale: KPI comparability depends on denominators and definitions. Source: MAIC Understanding Digital Journalism, page 9.

questions.stem: What might very high clicks but low article completion suggest?
options: The reporting is proven accurate
Every reader was satisfied
The story necessarily served the greatest public interest
Headline-content mismatch requiring investigation
questions.rationale: Clicks and completion can signal different audience behavior. Source: MAIC Understanding Digital Journalism, page 9.

questions.stem: Why should a public safety update not be judged by entertainment metrics alone?
options: Safety updates never have any audience
Useful information can matter even with fewer views
Only sensational stories can create public value
Engagement is a direct measure of harm prevention
questions.rationale: Public benefit extends beyond reach. Source: MAIC Understanding Digital Journalism, page 9.

questions.stem: An article records 300 completions among 1000 defined visits. What is its completion fraction?
questions.rationale: 300 divided by 1000 equals 0.30 or 30 percent. Source: MAIC Understanding Digital Journalism, page 9.

questions.stem: Why can a tracking-method change create apparent KPI improvement?
options: All methods always report identical counts
A method change always increases accuracy
Recorded numbers may change without any newsroom or audience behavior change
Data tracking is unrelated to analytics
questions.rationale: Measurement changes can confound trends. Source: MAIC Understanding Digital Journalism, page 9.

questions.stem: What is an example of a balancing quality measure?
options: Headline length alone
Advertising impressions alone
Social reactions alone
Factual corrections alongside total reach
questions.rationale: Quality metrics reveal harms hidden by attention. Source: MAIC Understanding Digital Journalism, page 9.

questions.stem: Why do chart axes need explicit units and time periods?
options: All numerical charts are self-explanatory
Units matter only for price charts
Readers need to know what was measured and when
An unlabeled graph proves a trend
questions.rationale: Data presentation must preserve definitions. Source: MAIC Understanding Digital Journalism, page 9.

questions.stem: What does a rise in two correlated metrics establish?
options: One metric definitely caused the other
Every other factor is irrelevant
An association that needs investigation before claiming cause
The sample is automatically representative
questions.rationale: Correlation is not proof of causation. Source: MAIC Understanding Digital Journalism, page 9.

questions.stem: Why should audience segments be interpreted carefully?
options: Every audience group has identical needs
Different reader mixes can alter aggregate performance
Segmentation guarantees causal proof
More segments always make a metric reliable
questions.rationale: Composition and context affect interpretation. Source: MAIC Understanding Digital Journalism, page 9.

questions.stem: What should a digital correction identify?
options: Only an apology without stating the fact
Only the new article image
Only how many readers complained
The material error, verified replacement and update date
questions.rationale: Corrections should be specific and traceable. Source: MAIC Understanding Digital Journalism, page 10.

questions.stem: Why is silent revision of a major error risky?
options: All readers automatically see updates
Deleted errors cannot persist in screenshots
Digital corrections are never needed
Earlier readers may rely on a different false version
questions.rationale: Past copies and impressions can remain influential. Source: MAIC Understanding Digital Journalism, page 10.

questions.stem: What should be checked after correcting a misleading web headline?
options: Whether related social previews and snippets still repeat the error
Only the office printer settings
Only the unrelated old articles
Only the author's biography
questions.rationale: The correction should address circulating false copies. Source: MAIC Understanding Digital Journalism, page 10.

questions.stem: Why should access to source files be controlled?
options: Access controls make every document true
Anyone online has a right to every private identifier
Login protection removes legal responsibilities
Sensitive information could expose sources or unreleased reporting
questions.rationale: Source confidentiality may require security safeguards. Source: MAIC Understanding Digital Journalism, page 10.

questions.stem: What hidden data can images potentially expose?
options: Only the image file extension
Location or identity information embedded in metadata or visible details
Only the editor's font choice
Only how many views it will receive
questions.rationale: Metadata and background details can reveal sensitive context. Source: MAIC Understanding Digital Journalism, page 10.

questions.stem: What is an AI transcription risk illustrated by 15 versus 50 buses?
options: Every AI transcript is more accurate than audio
Numbers are irrelevant to news reporting
Audio cannot be used to verify a quote
The tool can introduce a material numerical error
questions.rationale: AI outputs must be compared to original recordings. Source: MAIC Understanding Digital Journalism, page 10.

questions.stem: When could synthetic reconstruction mislead?
options: When clearly labeled as a hypothetical illustration
When excluded from the news report
When it is presented as authentic eyewitness footage
When described as computer-generated context
questions.rationale: Synthetic scenes must not be disguised as real documentation. Source: MAIC Understanding Digital Journalism, page 10.

questions.stem: Why should sensitive source documents not be sent to arbitrary AI services?
options: All AI systems automatically preserve attorney-client privilege
The document's spelling may change
Unapproved processing can create privacy and confidentiality exposure
Every upload converts a file to public domain
questions.rationale: Sensitive inputs need appropriate data handling. Source: MAIC Understanding Digital Journalism, page 10.

questions.stem: What is the proper response to an AI summary mentioning a source absent from the original?
options: Treat it as a newly discovered witness
Attribute it to the reporter
Publish it as a verified independent confirmation
Remove or investigate the unsupported source before publication
questions.rationale: Generated content cannot create evidence. Source: MAIC Understanding Digital Journalism, page 10.

questions.stem: When should serious digital legal or safety risks be escalated?
options: Before release to suitable qualified reviewers
Only after a publication is widely shared
Never for online media
Only when the image file is large
questions.rationale: High-risk material may require specialist review. Source: MAIC Understanding Digital Journalism, page 10.

questions.stem: What does the hypothetical bridge authority notice actually support?
options: A confirmed major fire
An indefinite full-bridge shutdown
A scheduled single-lane maintenance closure
A citywide transport emergency
questions.rationale: The notice is specifically about one lane and scheduled maintenance. Source: MAIC Understanding Digital Journalism, page 11.

questions.stem: Why does the older smoke photo not confirm a current fire?
options: It depicts a different earlier event
It includes a bridge
The smoke is visible
It was reposted recently
questions.rationale: A real image can be recycled with false event context. Source: MAIC Understanding Digital Journalism, page 11.

questions.stem: What should be checked before accepting the short fire video?
options: Only the number of reposts
Its original recording, time, location and independent evidence
Only its dramatic sound
Only the account's display name
questions.rationale: The clip has insufficient provenance in the case. Source: MAIC Understanding Digital Journalism, page 11.

questions.stem: Which headline is accurate under the fictional authority notice?
options: Major fire closes bridge indefinitely
Entire bridge has permanently collapsed
Transport authority confirms citywide emergency
One bridge lane scheduled to close for maintenance Tuesday through Thursday
questions.rationale: The verified announcement concerns a limited scheduled closure. Source: MAIC Understanding Digital Journalism, page 11.

questions.stem: What should a newsroom say about the claimed fire before confirmation?
options: It is a proven fact
It is confirmed by the older image
It is unverified and not established by the maintenance notice
It must be the reason for the maintenance schedule
questions.rationale: The rumor is not verified by the available primary source. Source: MAIC Understanding Digital Journalism, page 11.

questions.stem: What makes the hypothetical case a public-service reporting task?
options: It has a dramatic photograph
It was mentioned by an anonymous account
Travelers need accurate lane, date and route details
It could produce more engagement
questions.rationale: Accurate practical instructions serve readers. Source: MAIC Understanding Digital Journalism, page 11.

questions.stem: What should a claim table show for the indefinite-closure allegation?
options: A fully verified closure
A completed source audit confirming the claim
No supporting primary record and an unresolved verification need
A mandatory instruction to use the viral headline
questions.rationale: Evidence status must be tracked claim by claim. Source: MAIC Understanding Digital Journalism, page 11.

questions.stem: If a published report says two lanes close but notice says one, what is needed?
options: A visible correction to one lane with verified source context
Silent removal of every road reference
Keep two lanes because the rumor is popular
Claim all records are equally accurate
questions.rationale: The inaccurate lane count is a material service error. Source: MAIC Understanding Digital Journalism, page 11.

questions.stem: When should a new emergency update be published as factual?
options: When the repost count doubles
Whenever the old smoke image becomes popular
Immediately when an anonymous comment appears
After the relevant emergency information is independently verified
questions.rationale: Developing news requires checks before definitive updates. Source: MAIC Understanding Digital Journalism, page 11.

questions.stem: Which reporting choice best reduces avoidable harm in the bridge case?
